walkthrough.text:
Use conjugate root theorem:
$$\text{Since } p, q \in \mathbb{R}, z_2 = \bar{z}_1 = 4 + 3\mathrm{i}$$

Apply Vieta's formulas:
$$p = -(z_1 + z_2) = -8$$
$$q = z_1 z_2 = (4 - 3\mathrm{i})(4 + 3\mathrm{i}) = 16 + 9 = 25$$

Calculate area of triangle $OAB$:
$$\text{Base } AB = 8, \quad \text{Height } h = 2$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}(8)(2) = 8$$

walkthrough.text:
Take square roots of $u_1$ and $u_2$ in polar form:
$$z = \pm 2\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\pi}{3}\mathrm{i}} \quad \text{and} \quad z = \pm 2\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\pi}{3}\mathrm{i}}$$

walkthrough.text:
Find square roots of $8\mathrm{i}$:
$$(u + \mathrm{i}v)^2 = 8\mathrm{i} \implies u = v = \pm 2 \implies \sqrt{\Delta} = \pm(2 + 2\mathrm{i})$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Polar roots and integer powers.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding polar form of quadratic roots.
Finding smallest integer power for real value.

hints: Imaginary part is zero when $\frac{n\pi}{6} = k\pi \implies n = 6k$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply de Moivre's theorem to $z_1^n$:
$$z_1^n = (2\sqrt{3})^n \mathrm{e}^{\frac{n\pi}{6}\mathrm{i}}$$
$$\text{For } z_1^n \in \mathbb{R}, \sin\left(\frac{n\pi}{6}\right) = 0 \implies \frac{n\pi}{6} = k\pi \implies n = 6k$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Square roots and solving complex quadratic.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding square roots of -5 + 12i.

walkthrough.text:
Equate real and imaginary parts:
$$x^2 - y^2 = -5, \quad 2xy = 12 \implies y = \frac{6}{x}$$
$$x^2 - \frac{36}{x^2} = -5 \implies x^4 + 5x^2 - 36 = 0$$

Solve for $x$ and $y$:
$$(x^2 + 9)(x^2 - 4) = 0 \implies x^2 = 4 \implies x = \pm 2, \quad y = \pm 3$$
$$\text{Roots: } \pm(2 + 3\mathrm{i})$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving complex quadratic using precomputed square roots.

walkthrough.text:
Apply quadratic formula using square roots from part (a):
$$z = \frac{(2 + \mathrm{i}) \pm (2 + 3\mathrm{i})}{2}$$
$$z_1 = \frac{4 + 4\mathrm{i}}{2} = 2 + 2\mathrm{i}, \quad z_2 = \frac{-2\mathrm{i}}{2} = -\mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies quadratic formula with square root from part (a).

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Geometric quadrilateral formed by roots of two quadratics.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding Cartesian roots of two quadratics.

walkthrough.text:
Solve first quadratic equation:
$$z = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 - 20}}{2} = 1 \pm 2\mathrm{i} \implies z_1 = 1 + 2\mathrm{i}, \quad z_2 = 1 - 2\mathrm{i}$$

Solve second quadratic equation:
$$w = \frac{6 \pm \sqrt{36 - 100}}{2} = 3 \pm 4\mathrm{i} \implies w_1 = 3 + 4\mathrm{i}, \quad w_2 = 3 - 4\mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Correctly assigns labels according to imaginary parts.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving quadrilateral is trapezium and finding parallel side lengths.

hints: $z_1 z_2$ lies on $x = 1$, $w_1 w_2$ lies on $x = 3$. Both are vertical lines.

walkthrough.text:
Analyse side orientations:
$$z_1(1, 2) \text{ and } z_2(1, -2) \text{ lie on } x = 1$$
$$w_1(3, 4) \text{ and } w_2(3, -4) \text{ lie on } x = 3$$
$$\text{Both segments are vertical, so } z_1 z_2 \parallel w_1 w_2, \text{ proving the quadrilateral is a trapezium.}$$

Calculate parallel side lengths:
$$z_1 z_2 = |2 - (-2)| = 4, \quad w_1 w_2 = |4 - (-4)| = 8$$

ai_rubric.observable: Notes both $z_1 z_2$ and $w_1 w_2$ are vertical lines.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Calculating exact area of quadrilateral in Argand diagram.

hints: Distance between vertical lines $x = 1$ and $x = 3$ is $h = 3 - 1 = 2$.

walkthrough.text:
Find perpendicular height between parallel vertical sides:
$$h = 3 - 1 = 2$$
